Reproducing Valero et al. (2022) from dandiset 000568¶

Paper. Valero M, Zutshi I, Yoon E, Buzsaki G (2022). Probing subthreshold dynamics of hippocampal neurons by pulsed optogenetics. Science 375, 570-574. doi:10.1126/science.abm1891. This attempt used the full text of the NIH author manuscript in PubMed Central (PMC9632609): the main report and its figure legends. The Materials and Methods and figures S1 to S15 are in the supplement, which could not be obtained (PMC's copy is behind a captcha and the publisher's is not open access). Claims about supplementary figures are taken from the main text's statements of them, and method details come from the code named below.

Dandiset. DANDI:000568, version 0.230705.1633, streamed. The paper cites no DANDI version; its data statement points to the Buzsaki Lab Databank, whose page lists this dandiset for the paper (its other copy is on Globus, which needs an account and has no pinned identifier, so it was not used). This is the only published version. The draft holds the same 138 assets (paths, sizes and asset ids, printed below), so nothing the analysis uses differs.

What the dandiset holds. 28 sessions from 4 mice, each deposited twice (a full file and a no-raw-data file with the same units). Units carry spike times only, with no cell type. There are epochs, ripple intervals and linearized position. Laps and uLED pulse times are in 2 sessions only (fCamk1 sess9 and sess12), so every claim that needs light responses or place fields is tested on these two sessions of one mouse.

Code read. The paper names buzcode (github.com/buzsakilab/buzcode, commit e615663): the lab's general toolbox, with place-field and ripple functions but no script for this paper's figures. Its field rule (bz_findPlaceFields1D) is ported here with its defaults. The first author's later lab code, HippoCookBook (github.com/valegarman/HippoCookBook, commit 0cbded3), is not cited by the paper. It holds the light-response test (getuLEDResponse.m) used here. Whether either matches the paper's Methods could not be checked, as the Methods were not available.

Outside inputs. None.

The run takes about seven minutes, most of it streaming the files.

import time
import warnings

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats

import valero as v

pd.set_option("display.width", 220)
pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 40)
pd.set_option("display.max_rows", 200)
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=RuntimeWarning)


def ci95(k, n):
    """Clopper-Pearson 95% interval of a fraction k/n, in percent."""
    r = stats.binomtest(int(k), int(n)).proportion_ci()
    return f"{100 * r.low:.1f} to {100 * r.high:.1f}%"

started = time.time()
assets = v.assets()
small = [a for a in assets if "no-raw-data" in a["path"]]
full = {v.session_key(a["path"]): a for a in assets if "no-raw-data" not in a["path"]}
sessions = v.load_sessions([a["url"] for a in small])
for a, s in zip(small, sessions):
    s["key"] = v.session_key(a["path"])
    s["full_url"] = full[s["key"]]["url"] if s["key"] in full else None
from dandi.dandiapi import DandiAPIClient
with DandiAPIClient() as client:
    listing = {ver: {(a.path, a.size, a.identifier) for a in client.get_dandiset(v.DANDISET_ID, ver).get_assets()}
               for ver in (v.DANDISET_VERSION, "draft")}
    published = [x.identifier for x in client.get_dandiset(v.DANDISET_ID).get_versions() if x.identifier != "draft"]
print("Published versions:", published, "; assets in", v.DANDISET_VERSION, len(listing[v.DANDISET_VERSION]),
      "; in the draft", len(listing["draft"]), "; same paths, sizes and asset ids:", listing[v.DANDISET_VERSION] == listing["draft"])
print(f"{len(assets)} NWB files in dandiset {v.DANDISET_ID} version {v.DANDISET_VERSION}; "
      f"loaded {len(sessions)} no-raw-data files in {time.time() - started:.0f} s")

# Every file, paired by session; a pair holds the same units, spikes, ripples and position
# when these fingerprints agree.
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
with ThreadPoolExecutor(16) as ex:
    prints = pd.DataFrame(list(ex.map(v.file_fingerprint, assets)))
prints["kind"] = np.where(prints.path.str.contains("no-raw-data"), "no_raw", "full")
prints["size_GB"] = [round(a["size"] / 1e9, 3) for a in assets]
cols = ["n_units", "n_spikes", "spike_index_sum", "spike_head_sum", "spike_tail_sum", "n_ripples",
        "ripple_sum", "n_position", "position_sum"]
# Files are paired by the session_id they hold (without "_no_raw_data"), not by their names.
pairs = prints.pivot(index="pair_key", columns="kind",
                     values=cols + ["size_GB", "has_raw", "has_lfp", "raw_s", "lfp_s", "last_epoch_end_s"])
same = pd.Series({k: all(np.isclose(pairs.loc[k, (c, "full")], pairs.loc[k, (c, "no_raw")]) for c in cols)
                  for k in pairs.index}, name="identical_content")
print("Files per kind:", prints.kind.value_counts().to_dict())
print("Sessions (by session_id):", prints.pair_key.nunique(), "; sessions with both files:",
      int(pairs[("n_units", "full")].notna().sum()))
print("Sessions whose two files hold the same units, spikes, ripples and position:", int(same.sum()), "of", len(same))
print("Subjects:", sorted(prints.subject.unique()))
print("Units table columns (distinct over all 56 files):", prints.units_columns.unique().tolist())
print("session_start_time values:", prints.session_start_time.unique().tolist())
print("\nFiles whose name lacks the session:",
      prints[~prints.path.str.contains("ses-")][["path", "session_id"]].values.tolist())
table = pd.DataFrame({"units": pairs[("n_units", "no_raw")], "spikes": pairs[("n_spikes", "no_raw")],
                      "ripples": pairs[("n_ripples", "no_raw")], "full_GB": pairs[("size_GB", "full")],
                      "session_s": pairs[("last_epoch_end_s", "full")].round(0),
                      "full_raw_s": pairs[("raw_s", "full")].round(0), "full_lfp_s": pairs[("lfp_s", "full")].round(0),
                      "identical": same})
print(table.to_string())
short = table[(table.full_raw_s.notna() & (table.full_raw_s < 0.95 * table.session_s)) |
              (table.full_lfp_s < 0.95 * table.session_s)]
print("\nFull files whose raw or LFP signal covers less than 95% of the session:", short.index.tolist())
print("Full files without a raw signal:", table[table.full_raw_s.isna()].index.tolist())

The dandiset holds 56 NWB files and 82 videos. The NWB files cover 28 sessions: each session is deposited twice, as a full file and a no-raw-data file. In all 28 the two files hold the same units, spike times, ripples and position (the fingerprints above agree), so each session is counted once and read from its no-raw-data file. Units carry spike times, a unit name, a cluster id and, in most files, the shank (group_id); no file gives a cell type. The full file of fCamk3 sess20 lacks the session in its name; the session_id inside it identifies it. The full file of fCamk3 sess17 is 28 MB: its raw signal covers 378 s and its LFP 6850 s of a 34621 s session. Six full files of fCamk1 have the LFP but no raw signal. In fCamk2 sess4 the signals run 16736 s, past the last epoch at 12781 s. session_start_time is 2016-03-15 in every file, while the session ids date the recordings to 2020 and 2021, so the start time is wrong.

# Epochs, laps, ripples and pulse series per session; baseline rates of the units.
rows = []
for s in sessions:
    e0 = s["epochs"][0]
    dur = e0["stop"] - e0["start"]
    s["base_rate"] = np.array([((x >= e0["start"]) & (x < e0["stop"])).sum() / dur for x in s["spikes"]])
    s["pyr"] = s["base_rate"] < v.PYR_MAX_RATE_HZ
    paradigms = [e.get("behavioral_paradigm", "") for e in s["epochs"]]
    manip = [e.get("manipulation", "") for e in s["epochs"]]
    s["stim_protocol"] = any("uled" in m.lower() for m in manip)
    rows.append({"session": s["key"].split("_ses-")[1], "subject": s["subject"], "units": len(s["spikes"]),
                 "putative_pyr": int(s["pyr"].sum()), "first_epoch_s": round(dur),
                 "epochs": len(s["epochs"]), "labelled": any(paradigms), "uLED_epochs": s["stim_protocol"],
                 "chemogenetic": any(("CNO" in p) or ("DMSO" in p) for p in paradigms),
                 "laps": len(s["laps"]), "ripples": len(s["ripples"]),
                 "pulse_series": len(s["pulses"]), "position_samples": len(s.get("pos_t", []))})
overview = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(overview.to_string(index=False))
print("\nSessions per subject:", overview.groupby("subject").size().to_dict())
print("Sessions with pulse times:", overview[overview.pulse_series > 0].session.tolist())
print("Sessions with laps:", overview[overview.laps > 0].session.tolist())
print("Sessions without epoch labels:", overview[~overview.labelled].session.tolist())
print("Sessions with CNO or DMSO epochs:", int(overview.chemogenetic.sum()))
print("\nEpoch names of each kind of session:")
for s in sessions:
    if s["key"].endswith(("fCamk1-200827-sess9", "fCamk3-201029-sess11-cleanned", "fCamk2-201012-sess1")):
        print(" ", s["key"], [(e.get("behavioral_paradigm") or e.get("epoch_name"), e.get("manipulation", "")) for e in s["epochs"]])

There are four subjects, matching the paper's four mice. Pulse times are deposited for 2 sessions only (fCamk1 sess9 and sess12). The other 20 sessions whose epochs name "uLED random stim" have no pulse times, so their light responses cannot be computed. Only the same two sessions have laps; position is present in 24 sessions. Six sessions (all four of fCamk2, fCamk3 sess13 and fCamk5 sess10) name their epochs only by a time stamp, without paradigm or manipulation. 14 sessions have a second block of epochs named CNO or DMSO, a chemogenetic manipulation that the paper does not describe. fCamk2 has no position and 0 to 1110 ripples per session.

# Baseline firing rates, and the putative pyramidal threshold.
rates = np.concatenate([s["base_rate"] for s in sessions])
print("Units:", len(rates), "; baseline rate percentiles 5/25/50/75/95 (Hz):",
      np.percentile(rates, [5, 25, 50, 75, 95]).round(2).tolist(), "; max", rates.max().round(1))
for thr in (2.5, 5, 10, 15):
    print(f"  below {thr:>4} Hz: {(rates < thr).sum()} units ({(rates < thr).mean():.1%})")
isi_viol = []
for s in sessions:
    for x in s["spikes"]:
        if len(x) > 100:
            isi_viol.append(np.mean(np.diff(x) < 0.002))
isi_viol = np.array(isi_viol)
print("Units whose spike times are not sorted:", sum(int(np.any(np.diff(x) < 0)) for s in sessions for x in s["spikes"]))
print("Fraction of ISIs below 2 ms per unit, percentiles 50/90/99:", np.percentile(isi_viol, [50, 90, 99]).round(4).tolist())
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 3))
ax.hist(np.log10(rates + 1e-3), bins=60, color="0.4")
ax.axvline(np.log10(v.PYR_MAX_RATE_HZ), color="C3", lw=1)
ax.set_xlabel("log10 baseline rate (Hz)")
ax.set_ylabel("units")
ax.set_title(f"all {len(rates)} units; red: {v.PYR_MAX_RATE_HZ} Hz")
plt.show()

The files carry no cell type. Baseline-epoch rates have a median of 1.05 Hz. 1351 of 1481 units (91.2%) are below 5 Hz, the threshold used here for putative pyramidal cells; with 2.5 or 10 Hz the count is 1205 or 1441. Spike times are sorted in every unit, and ISIs below 2 ms are rare (median 0.15% of a unit's ISIs, 99th percentile 2.6%).

# The two sessions with pulse times: the pulse series, their stated units and values, and the
# position and laps.
opto = [s for s in sessions if s["pulses"]]
for s in opto:
    print(s["key"])
    for site, p in s["pulses"].items():
        d = (p["off"] - p["on"]) * 1000
        print(f"  {site}: {len(p['on'])} pulses, stored value(s) {p['values'].tolist()} '{p['unit']}', "
              f"duration median {np.median(d):.2f} ms (range {d.min():.2f} to {d.max():.2f}), "
              f"first {p['on'][0]:.1f} s, last {p['on'][-1]:.1f} s")
    print("  stimulation epochs:", [(e["behavioral_paradigm"], round(e["start"]), round(e["stop"]))
                                    for e in s["epochs"] if "uLED" in e["manipulation"]])
    x = s["pos_x"]
    print(f"  linearized position: {len(x)} samples, {np.nanmin(x):.1f} to {np.nanmax(x):.1f}, stated unit "
          f"{s['pos_attrs']['unit']!r} with conversion {s['pos_attrs']['conversion']}")
    laps = s["laps"]
    mz = v.epoch_interval(s, "Maze")[0]
    print(f"  laps: {len(laps)}, all inside the Maze epoch: {bool(np.all((laps[:, 0] >= mz[0]) & (laps[:, 1] <= mz[1])))}, "
          f"directions {np.unique(laps[:, 2], return_counts=True)[1].tolist()}, duration median {np.median(laps[:, 1] - laps[:, 0]):.1f} s")
    on = np.sort(np.concatenate([p["on"] for p in s["pulses"].values()]))
    per_lap = np.array([((on >= a) & (on < b)).sum() / (b - a) for a, b, _ in laps])
    no_stim = np.flatnonzero(per_lap < 1) + 1
    print(f"  laps with fewer than 1 pulse/s (numbered from 1): {no_stim.tolist()}")
    start_x = np.interp(laps[:, 0], s["pos_t"], s["pos_x"])
    stop_x = np.interp(laps[:, 1], s["pos_t"], s["pos_x"])
    for d in (0, 1):
        k = laps[:, 2] == d
        print(f"  direction {d}: position at lap start median {np.median(start_x[k]):.1f}, at lap end median {np.median(stop_x[k]):.1f}")

The pulse series are stated in watts but hold one value per uLED: 19 in sess9 and 62623 to 63599 in sess12. These cannot be watts (the paper gives 0.02 to 0.1 uW), and with one value per uLED they carry no intensity levels. Each pulse is four samples (off, on, on, off) spanning 19.87 ms (sess9) or 19.63 ms (sess12), consistent with the paper's 20 ms pulses. The files hold series for six uLEDs (Site3 to Site8) of the probe's twelve; Site6 and Site7 have only 120 to 221 pulses. The next check shows that most pulses are not in the files.

The linearized position runs from 0 to 110, the track's length in cm, but carries a conversion factor of 100, which would make it 0 to 110 m; the conversion is wrong. Laps lie inside the Maze epoch and alternate direction, starting and ending near the track ends. Three blocks of laps have no pulses (sess9: laps 1-11, 52-61, 102-111; sess12: 1-10, 61-70, 121-132), the baseline runs of the paper's design. In sess9 they are not at laps 61-70 and 121-130 as in Figure 3F's legend.

The device holds 12 uLEDs, 3 per shank, and the files hold pulse series for six of them (Site3 to Site8), all with the same description. Most pulses of the protocol are not in the files. In PreStim the deposited pulses come at 5.76 and 7.50 per s, where 20 ms pulses separated by 20 to 40 ms offsets would come at 17 to 25 per s. In sess9 the offsets between consecutive deposited pulses fall only near 20, 40, 60, 80, 100 ms and so on (5 ms bins above). An offset of 60 ms is a 20 ms offset, a 20 ms pulse and another 20 ms offset, so a pulse lies in it that is not in the file. In sess12, 30.2% of offsets fall within 20 to 40 ms, 5.5% within 40 to 60 ms, and 20.3% within 60 to 100 ms, the range of one missing pulse with its two offsets. No putative pyramidal cell on shank Group3 responds to any deposited uLED (fig1e section), so that shank's uLEDs are likely among the missing ones.

Under the stated protocol the next pulse at any site starts 20 to 40 ms after the end of the last, so the 20 ms before each deposited onset and the 20 ms after each deposited offset are dark. The files do not follow this exactly: 3.8% (sess9) and 3.2% (sess12) of the end-to-start offsets between deposited pulses in PreStim are under 20 ms, nearly all of them under 10 ms or negative. Deposited pulses are cut out of these windows, but pulses missing from the files may fall in them as often. From here on, control time for rate maps and in-field rates is restricted to these windows (about 20% of lap time, printed below). All time without a deposited pulse (88% to 90% of lap time) may hold the light of missing pulses, and is shown as a variant. The 20 ms control windows before each onset, used for fig1i and fig2b, are dark under the protocol.

# Clock checks. (1) Light responses: the population PSTH around the pulse onsets of each uLED,
# against the same onsets shifted by 250 ms. (2) Ripples: the population rate in the deposited
# ripple intervals against the same intervals shifted by 1 s, in every session with ripples.
for s in opto:
    pyr_spk = [x for x, p in zip(s["spikes"], s["pyr"]) if p]
    pre = v.epoch_interval(s, "PreStim")[0]
    for site, p in s["pulses"].items():
        on = p["on"][(p["on"] >= pre[0]) & (p["on"] < pre[1])]
        if len(on) < v.MIN_PULSES:
            continue
        true = np.mean([v.count_in_windows(x, on, 0.02).sum() for x in pyr_spk]) / len(on) / 0.02
        before = np.mean([v.count_in_windows(x, on - 0.02, 0.02).sum() for x in pyr_spk]) / len(on) / 0.02
        shifted = np.mean([v.count_in_windows(x, on + 0.25, 0.02).sum() for x in pyr_spk]) / len(on) / 0.02
        print(f"{s['key'].split('_ses-')[1]} {site}: mean pyramidal rate 0-20 ms after onset {true:.2f} Hz, "
              f"20 ms before {before:.2f} Hz, onsets shifted by 250 ms {shifted:.2f} Hz")
rip_rows = []
for s in sessions:
    r = s["ripples"]
    if len(r) < 50:
        continue
    allspk = np.sort(np.concatenate(s["spikes"]))
    dur = (r[:, 1] - r[:, 0]).sum()
    inside = (np.searchsorted(allspk, r[:, 1]) - np.searchsorted(allspk, r[:, 0])).sum() / dur
    sh = (np.searchsorted(allspk, r[:, 1] + 1) - np.searchsorted(allspk, r[:, 0] + 1)).sum() / dur
    rip_rows.append({"session": s["key"].split("_ses-")[1], "ripples": len(r),
                     "duration_ms_median": round(1000 * np.median(r[:, 1] - r[:, 0]), 1),
                     "peak_inside": bool(np.all((r[:, 2] >= r[:, 0]) & (r[:, 2] <= r[:, 1]))),
                     "pop_rate_in_ripples": round(inside, 1), "pop_rate_shifted_1s": round(sh, 1)})
rip_check = pd.DataFrame(rip_rows)
print(rip_check.to_string(index=False))
print("Sessions where the population rate inside ripples is at least twice the shifted rate:",
      int((rip_check.pop_rate_in_ripples > 2 * rip_check.pop_rate_shifted_1s).sum()), "of", len(rip_check))

Sessions where the population rate inside ripples is at least twice the shifted rate: 22 of 25

Pulse onsets share the clock of the spikes: for every uLED tested, the mean rate of the putative pyramidal cells in the 20 ms after onset is above the rate in the 20 ms before (by 0.10 to 1.25 Hz). For 6 of 8 it is also above the rate in the same window 250 ms later. The other two are sess12 Site3 and Site5, and the later window often holds pulses of other uLEDs. Responses per unit are tested under fig1e. The deposited ripples share the clock of the spikes: the population rate inside them is at least twice the rate 1 s later in 22 of 25 sessions with ripples. In fCamk3 sess13 (1.3 times), fCamk3 sess17 (1.98 times) and fCamk5 sess10 (1.2 times; 217 events with a median duration of 109 ms) the ripple intervals mark population bursts weakly. The LFP clock is checked in the fig2b section: the stored LFP rate is 1250 Hz from 0 s, the LFP and the raw signal both end with the last epoch, and ripple-band power at the deposited ripple peaks is 194 and 248 times its mean in BaselinePre and 113 and 78 times inside the Maze epoch. Position shares the clock of the laps (lap ends at track ends, above).

# Responsiveness of every unit to every uLED, in the PreStim epoch (main) and over all
# stimulation epochs (reading b of fig1e). One generator per session.
for i, s in enumerate(opto):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(1000 + i)
    pre = v.epoch_interval(s, "PreStim")[0]
    s["resp_table"] = pd.DataFrame(v.responsive_sites(s, pre, rng))
    stim = [(e["start"], e["stop"]) for e in s["epochs"] if "uLED" in e["manipulation"]]
    whole = (min(a for a, _ in stim), max(b for _, b in stim))
    s["resp_table_all"] = pd.DataFrame(v.responsive_sites(s, whole, rng))
    t = s["resp_table"]
    s["resp_sites"] = {u: sorted(g[g.responsive.fillna(False).astype(bool)].site) for u, g in t.groupby("unit")}
    s["responsive"] = np.array([len(s["resp_sites"].get(u, [])) > 0 for u in range(len(s["spikes"]))])
    s["tested_sites"] = sorted(t[t.tested].site.unique())
    print(s["key"], "tested uLEDs:", s["tested_sites"], "; responsive units:", int(s["responsive"].sum()),
          "of", len(s["spikes"]), "; responsive putative pyramidal:", int((s["responsive"] & s["pyr"]).sum()),
          "of", int(s["pyr"].sum()))

Claim cohort-counts¶

CA1 pyramidal neurons were recorded and probed in four CaMKIIa-Cre::Ai32 mice, 822 pyramidal neurons in all, 43.3 plus or minus 8.37 per session.

def cohort(rows):
    return {"sessions": len(rows), "mice": rows.subject.nunique(), "pyramidal": int(rows.putative_pyr.sum()),
            "per_session_mean": round(rows.putative_pyr.mean(), 1), "per_session_sd": round(rows.putative_pyr.std(), 2)}

readings = {"(a) all sessions": overview, "(b) sessions naming the uLED protocol": overview[overview.uLED_epochs]}
res = pd.DataFrame({k: cohort(r) for k, r in readings.items()}).T
res["mice_ok"] = res.mice == 4
res["total_ok"] = (res.pyramidal - 822).abs() <= 82
res["mean_ok"] = (res.per_session_mean - 43.3).abs() <= 8.37
print(res.to_string())

Result: partially reproduced. Under reading (a), all 28 sessions, the dandiset holds 4 mice and 48.2 putative pyramidal cells per session (SD 12.18), within 43.3 plus or minus 8.37, but 1351 in all, against 822 plus or minus 82. Under reading (b), the 22 sessions naming the uLED protocol, it holds 3 mice (fCamk2 has no epoch labels), 1047 cells and 47.6 per session. At 43.3 per session, 822 cells would come from about 19 sessions; the dandiset holds 28 and does not say which the paper used. The thresholds 2.5 and 10 Hz give 1205 and 1441 cells under reading (a).

Claim fig1c-pulse-protocol¶

uLEDs were driven with 20 ms pulses at random sites with randomly variable 20 to 40 ms offsets, so that the stimulation of each site recurred at about 0.3 to 0.6 s intervals.

rows = []
for s in opto:
    stim = [(e["start"], e["stop"]) for e in s["epochs"] if "uLED" in e["manipulation"]]
    allon = []
    for site, p in s["pulses"].items():
        keep = np.zeros(len(p["on"]), bool)
        for a, b in stim:
            keep |= (p["on"] >= a) & (p["on"] < b)
        on, off = p["on"][keep], p["off"][keep]
        allon.append(np.column_stack([on, off]))
        ipi = np.diff(on)
        rows.append({"session": s["key"].split("_ses-")[1], "uLED": site, "pulses": len(on),
                     "duration_ms": round(1000 * np.median(off - on), 2),
                     "interval_median_s": round(np.median(ipi), 3),
                     "interval_5_95_s": np.percentile(ipi, [5, 95]).round(3).tolist(),

    iv = np.concatenate(allon)
    iv = iv[np.argsort(iv[:, 0])]
    gap = (iv[1:, 0] - iv[:-1, 1]) * 1000
    print(f"{s['key'].split('_ses-')[1]}: offset from the end of a pulse to the start of the next (any uLED), "
          f"median {np.median(gap):.1f} ms, 5th to 95th percentile {np.percentile(gap, 5):.1f} to {np.percentile(gap, 95):.1f} ms, "
          f"overlapping pulses {int((gap < 0).sum())} of {len(gap)}; within 20 to 40 ms {np.mean((gap >= 20) & (gap <= 40)):.1%}, "
          f"within 40 to 60 ms (file description) {np.mean((gap >= 40) & (gap <= 60)):.1%}; onset to next onset "
          f"within 40 to 60 ms {np.mean((np.diff(iv[:, 0]) >= 0.04) & (np.diff(iv[:, 0]) <= 0.06)):.1%}")
    s["gap_ms"] = gap

Result: partially reproduced. Pulses last 19.75 ms (median over uLEDs), and the median interval between pulses of one uLED is 0.281 to 0.383 s for the four uLEDs with at least 1000 pulses, both as the paper states. The median offset from the end of one pulse to the start of the next is 60.4 ms in sess9 and 80.0 ms in sess12, outside 18 to 44 ms. Of these offsets 31.8% and 30.2% fall within 20 to 40 ms, and the 95th percentiles are 241 and 328 ms. The data check shows that most pulses are not in the files (5.76 and 7.50 deposited pulses per s in PreStim, and offsets in sess9 near multiples of 20 ms only), so the longer offsets span missing pulses, and the protocol's offsets cannot be measured from the files. Measured onset to onset, the same 31.8% and 30.2% fall within the 40 to 60 ms of the file's description, so the paper's range and the file's agree if the file's is onset to onset.

Result: reproduced under reading (b). Over all stimulation epochs, 66 of 91 putative pyramidal cells (72.5%, 95% interval 62.2 to 81.4%) respond to at least one uLED, within 74.3 plus or minus 7.4%. Under reading (a), the PreStim epoch alone, 57 of 91 (62.6%, 51.9 to 72.6%) do, outside tolerance. Of 364 unit and uLED tests in PreStim, 68 pass all three parts of the test. On sham onsets, jittered by up to 200 ms or moved into BaselinePre, none of the 364 PreStim tests passes. For reading (b), onsets over all stimulation epochs jittered by up to 200 ms, none of 364 tests passes either. No putative pyramidal cell on shank Group3 responds (0 of 8 and 0 of 9), while the other shanks respond each to their own uLEDs (Site3 and Site4 on Group1, Site5 on Group2, Site8 on Group4). The uLEDs of Group3 are likely among those whose pulses are not in the files, so some cells counted as non-responsive may respond to light that cannot be tested here. Without Group3, 57 of 74 (77.0%) respond under reading (a), within tolerance, and 66 of 74 (89.2%) under reading (b), above it. These are two sessions of one mouse, not the paper's 822 cells.

Claim fig1i-swr-decrease¶

def overlaps(starts, width, iv):
    # whether [start, start + width) overlaps any interval of iv (sorted by start)
    j = np.searchsorted(iv[:, 0], starts + width) - 1
    ok = j >= 0
    out = np.zeros(len(starts), bool)
    out[ok] = iv[j[ok], 1] > starts[ok]
    return out

rows = []

    ctrl = v.restrict(s["control"], home)
    c_in = overlaps(ctrl, v.CONTROL_WINDOW_S, rip)
    for u in np.flatnonzero(s["responsive"] & s["pyr"]):
        on = v.restrict(s["cell_onsets"][u], home)
        l_in = overlaps(on, v.PULSE_WINDOW_S, rip)

        lc, cc = v.count_in_windows(x, on, 0.02), v.count_in_windows(x, ctrl, 0.02)
        rows.append({"session": s["key"].split("_ses-")[1], "unit": u,

Result: reproduced. In 57 light-responsive putative pyramidal cells, the light minus control rate is 0.30 Hz (median) in windows overlapping ripples and 2.68 Hz outside them. It is lower inside ripples in 49 of 57 cells (Wilcoxon p = 6.8e-09), and in each session (p = 7.8e-06 and 9.5e-07). As a ratio, light over control is 1.25 inside and 2.89 outside (53 of 56 lower, p = 8.6e-10). The control windows, the 20 ms before each onset, are dark under the protocol, so the missing pulses do not enter them. The paper's n of 485 and P < 1e-55 are out of reach of two sessions.

    t_in = (r[:, 1] - r[:, 0]).sum()
    t_out = (e0["stop"] - e0["start"]) - t_in
    for u in np.flatnonzero(s["pyr"]):
        x = s["spikes"][u]
        n_all = ((x >= e0["start"]) & (x < e0["stop"])).sum()
        n_in = (np.searchsorted(x, r[:, 1]) - np.searchsorted(x, r[:, 0])).sum()
        rows.append({"session": s["key"].split("_ses-")[1], "subject": s["subject"], "base": n_all / (e0["stop"] - e0["start"]),
                     "in": n_in / t_in, "out": (n_all - n_in) / t_out, "ripples": len(r)})
g = pd.DataFrame(rows)
g["log2_ratio"] = np.log2(g["in"] / g["out"])
g["diff"] = g["in"] - g["out"]
print("Sessions:", g.session.nunique(), "; putative pyramidal cells:", len(g),
      "; cells with no spikes in ripples (left out of reading a):", int((g["in"] == 0).sum()))
for name, col in (("(a) log2 ratio in/out", "log2_ratio"), ("(b) difference in - out", "diff")):
    k = g[np.isfinite(g[col])]
    rho = stats.spearmanr(k[col], k.base)
    print(f"{name}: n = {len(k)}, rho = {rho.statistic:.3f}, p = {rho.pvalue:.2g}, "
          f"within -0.19 +- 0.068: {abs(rho.statistic + 0.19) <= 0.068}")
print("\nPer subject and per session, reading (a):")
k = g[np.isfinite(g.log2_ratio)]
for key, grp in list(k.groupby("subject")) + list(k.groupby("session")):
    rr = stats.spearmanr(grp.log2_ratio, grp.base)
    print(f"  {key}: n = {len(grp)}, rho = {rr.statistic:.2f}, p = {rr.pvalue:.2g}")
bad = rip_check[rip_check.pop_rate_in_ripples < 2 * rip_check.pop_rate_shifted_1s].session.tolist()
kk = k[~k.session.isin(bad)]
rr = stats.spearmanr(kk.log2_ratio, kk.base)
print(f"Variant, without the sessions whose ripples fail the clock check {bad}: n = {len(kk)}, rho = {rr.statistic:.3f}, p = {rr.pvalue:.2g}")
labelled = [s["key"].split("_ses-")[1] for s in sessions if s["epochs"][0].get("behavioral_paradigm") == "BaselinePre"]
kl = k[k.session.isin(labelled)]
rr = stats.spearmanr(kl.log2_ratio, kl.base)
print(f"Variant, sessions whose first epoch is labelled BaselinePre ({kl.session.nunique()} sessions): n = {len(kl)}, rho = {rr.statistic:.3f}, p = {rr.pvalue:.2g}")
kk = g[g.ripples >= 1000]
kk = kk[np.isfinite(kk.log2_ratio)]

Result: partially reproduced. Over 1166 putative pyramidal cells of 24 sessions, the log2 ratio of the rate inside ripples to the rate outside is negatively correlated with the baseline rate, rho = -0.437 (p = 1.8e-55). It is negative in every subject (-0.37 to -0.71) and every session, and significant (p < 0.05) in all sessions but three (fCamk1 sess13, p = 0.12; fCamk3 sess13, p = 0.29; fCamk5 sess14, p = 0.81). Over all cells it is stronger than the paper's -0.19 plus or minus 0.068. Under the other reading, the difference inside minus outside, rho = -0.002 (p = 0.95). Without the two sessions in this analysis whose ripples fail the clock check (fCamk3 sess13 and sess17; the third, fCamk5 sess10, has under 50 ripples in its first epoch), n = 1055 and rho = -0.468; in the 22 sessions whose first epoch is labelled BaselinePre, rho = -0.450; against the rate outside ripples, which shares no spikes with the rate inside, rho = -0.466. Which measure of change the paper used is not known, and the two readings disagree.

Claim fig2b-theta-trough-gain¶

During track running, the light-induced rate gain is largest at the trough of the theta cycle (P < 1e-6, Wilcoxon test).

rows, check, lfp_checks = [], [], []
for s in opto:
    b0 = v.epoch_interval(s, "BaselinePre")[0]
    t0 = b0[0] + 600
    lfp = v.read_lfp(s["full_url"], t0, t0 + 300)
    peaks = s["ripples"][:, 2]
    peaks = peaks[(peaks > t0) & (peaks < t0 + 300)]
    ch = v.ripple_channel(lfp, t0, peaks)
    mz = v.epoch_interval(s, "Maze")[0]
    x = v.read_lfp(s["full_url"], mz[0], mz[1], [ch])[:, 0]
    phase = v.theta_phase(x)
    # clock check of the LFP: ripple-band power at ripple peaks against shifted peaks
    from scipy import signal as sg
    sos = sg.butter(3, v.RIPPLE_BAND, btype="band", fs=v.LFP_RATE, output="sos")
    y = sg.sosfiltfilt(sos, lfp[:, ch].astype(float)) ** 2
    ii = ((peaks - t0) * v.LFP_RATE).astype(int)
    ii = ii[(ii > 2000) & (ii < len(y) - 2000)]
    check.append((s["key"].split("_ses-")[1], ch, len(ii), y[ii].mean() / y.mean(), y[ii + 1250].mean() / y.mean()))
    # the same check inside the Maze epoch, on the channel used for theta
    ym = sg.sosfiltfilt(sos, x.astype(float)) ** 2
    pm = s["ripples"][:, 2]
    im = ((pm[(pm > mz[0]) & (pm < mz[1])] - mz[0]) * v.LFP_RATE).astype(int)
    im = im[(im > 2000) & (im < len(ym) - 2000)]
    # theta-band signal, for the phase convention and for light artifacts
    th_sos = sg.butter(3, v.THETA_BAND, btype="band", fs=v.LFP_RATE, output="sos")
    yt = sg.sosfiltfilt(th_sos, x.astype(float))
    lfp_checks.append({"session": s["key"].split("_ses-")[1], "ripples_in_maze": len(im),
                       "maze_power_at_peaks_x_mean": round(ym[im].mean() / ym.mean(), 1),
                       "maze_power_1s_later_x_mean": round(ym[im + 1250].mean() / ym.mean(), 1),
                       "yt": yt, "mz0": mz[0], "x": x})
    def ph(t):
        i = ((t - mz[0]) * v.LFP_RATE).astype(int)
        return phase[np.clip(i, 0, len(phase) - 1)]
    laps = s["laps"][:, :2]
    ctrl = s["control"][v.in_intervals(s["control"], laps)]
    c_ph = ph(ctrl + 0.01)
    for u in np.flatnonzero(s["responsive"] & s["pyr"]):
        on = s["cell_onsets"][u]
        on = on[v.in_intervals(on, laps)]
        l_ph = ph(on + 0.01)
        xs = s["spikes"][u]
        lc, cc = v.count_in_windows(xs, on, 0.02) / 0.02, v.count_in_windows(xs, ctrl, 0.02) / 0.02
        row = {"session": s["key"].split("_ses-")[1], "unit": u}
        trough_l, trough_c = np.abs(l_ph) > np.pi / 2, np.abs(c_ph) > np.pi / 2
        row["gain_trough"] = lc[trough_l].mean() - cc[trough_c].mean()
        row["gain_peak"] = lc[~trough_l].mean() - cc[~trough_c].mean()
        edges = np.linspace(-np.pi, np.pi, 7)
        for k in range(6):
            a = (l_ph >= edges[k]) & (l_ph < edges[k + 1])
            b = (c_ph >= edges[k]) & (c_ph < edges[k + 1])
            row[f"bin{k}"] = lc[a].mean() - cc[b].mean()
        rows.append(row)
for c in check:
    print(f"{c[0]}: LFP channel {c[1]}; ripple-band power at {c[2]} ripple peaks {c[3]:.1f} x the mean, "

Result: not reproduced. In 57 light-responsive putative pyramidal cells during laps, the gain (light minus control) is 2.04 Hz in the trough half of theta and 2.07 Hz in the peak half (medians). The trough is higher in 22 of 57 cells (Wilcoxon p = 0.14), and in neither session (p = 0.46 and 0.16). In 60-degree bins the median gain is largest at 30 degrees past the peak (2.13 Hz), and 1.88 and 1.92 Hz in the bins next to the trough. The checks above support the phase: the stored LFP rate is 1250 Hz from 0 s, ripple-band power at 44 and 27 deposited ripple peaks inside the Maze epoch is 113 and 78 times its mean, and spikes of putative pyramidal cells in control windows have a circular mean phase of 128 and 130 degrees, in the trough half, though weakly modulated (bin counts differ by at most 30%). Averaged around deposited onsets, the theta-band LFP deviates by at most 27.1 and 8.5 against a theta-band SD of 406 and 770, so light artifacts in the theta band are small. The LFP channel, band and phase convention are this attempt's choices, since the Methods were not available.

# Rate maps and place fields over the laps of the Maze epoch, per running direction.
for s in opto:
    grid = v.lap_grid(s, s["laps"])
    s["grid"] = grid
    on_any = v.in_intervals(grid["t"], s["light_iv"])
    # control time: windows dark under the protocol; all time without a deposited pulse is a variant
    s["ctrl_mask_nolight"] = ~on_any
    s["ctrl_mask"] = v.in_intervals(grid["t"], s["dark_iv"]) & ~on_any
    s["ctrl_maps"] = [v.rate_map(x, grid, s["ctrl_mask"]) for x in s["spikes"]]
    s["ctrl_fields"] = [[v.find_fields(m[d]) for d in (0, 1)] for m in s["ctrl_maps"]]
    s["place"] = np.array([any(len(f) for f in ff) for ff in s["ctrl_fields"]])
    # light masks: the cell's own uLEDs, and every tested uLED
    def mask_for(onsets):
        iv = np.column_stack([onsets, onsets + v.PULSE_WINDOW_S])
        return v.in_intervals(grid["t"], v.merge_intervals(iv))
    s["light_mask"] = {u: mask_for(on) for u, on in s["cell_onsets"].items()}
    s["all_light_mask"] = mask_for(s["all_tested_onsets"])
    s["light_maps"] = {u: v.rate_map(s["spikes"][u], grid, m) for u, m in s["light_mask"].items()}
    s["all_light_maps"] = [v.rate_map(x, grid, s["all_light_mask"]) for x in s["spikes"]]
    print(f"{s['key'].split('_ses-')[1]}: grid {len(grid['t'])} steps of {v.GRID_S * 1000:.0f} ms over {len(s['laps'])} laps; "
          f"control time (dark windows) {s['ctrl_mask'].mean():.1%}; time without a deposited pulse {s['ctrl_mask_nolight'].mean():.1%}; time in the light windows of all tested uLEDs {s['all_light_mask'].mean():.1%}; "
          f"place cells among putative pyramidal {int((s['place'] & s['pyr']).sum())} of {int(s['pyr'].sum())}")

    for rule_name, rule in (("buzcode port", v.find_fields), ("earlier rule", v.find_fields_simple)):
        pl = np.array([any(len(rule(m[d])) for d in (0, 1)) for m in maps.values()])
        tab_v = pd.crosstab(resp, pl).reindex(index=[False, True], columns=[False, True], fill_value=0).values
        var.append({"control time": mask_name, "field rule": rule_name, "place % responsive": round(100 * pl[resp].mean(), 1),
                    "place % non-responsive": round(100 * pl[~resp].mean(), 1), "place % all": round(100 * pl.mean(), 1),
                    "chi2 p": round(stats.chi2_contingency(tab_v).pvalue, 4),
                    "cells changed vs main": int((pl != pc.place.values).sum())})
print(pd.DataFrame(var).to_string(index=False))

Result: partially reproduced. 48 of 57 light-responsive putative pyramidal cells (84.2%, 95% interval 72.1 to 92.5%) and 24 of 34 non-responsive ones (70.6%, 52.5 to 84.9%) are place cells. The paper's chi-squared test finds no difference (p = 0.20), as in the paper. The non-responsive fraction is within tolerance of 71%; the responsive one is above 73 plus or minus 7.3%. In sess9, 83% of responsive and 56% of non-responsive cells are place cells; in sess12, 86% and 83%. Field peak thresholds of 1 and 3 Hz give 91.2% against 79.4%, and 73.7% against 61.8%. Over all putative pyramidal cells, 79.1% are place cells, more than half as stated. With all time without a deposited pulse as control time and the earlier field rule, the fractions are 78.9% and 52.9% (p = 0.018); the control time alone changes 5 cells, the field rule alone 1, and both together 11. Some non-responsive cells may respond to uLEDs whose pulses are not in the files (fig1e).

Claim fig2e-infield-gain¶

The light-induced rate increase is higher within than outside the place field (n = 553 place fields, P < 1e-115, Wilcoxon test).

In [18]:
def rate_where(x, grid, mask):
    # rate (Hz) of spikes falling in grid steps where mask holds
    i = np.searchsorted(grid["t"], x, side="right") - 1
    ok = (i >= 0) & (i < len(grid["t"]))
    i = i[ok][(x[ok] - grid["t"][i[ok]]) < v.GRID_S]
    t = mask.sum() * v.GRID_S
    return mask[i].sum() / t if t > 0 else np.nan, t

rows = []
for s in opto:
    grid = s["grid"]
    b = v.bin_index(grid["x"])
    for u in np.flatnonzero(s["responsive"] & s["pyr"] & s["place"]):
        for d in (0, 1):
            for (a, z, peak) in s["ctrl_fields"][u][d]:
                infield = (grid["dir"] == d) & (b >= a) & (b < z)
                outfield = (grid["dir"] == d) & ~((b >= a) & (b < z))
                li, lt = rate_where(s["spikes"][u], grid, s["light_mask"][u] & infield)
                ci, _ = rate_where(s["spikes"][u], grid, s["ctrl_mask"] & infield)
                lo, _ = rate_where(s["spikes"][u], grid, s["light_mask"][u] & outfield)
                co, _ = rate_where(s["spikes"][u], grid, s["ctrl_mask"] & outfield)
                rows.append({"session": s["key"].split("_ses-")[1], "unit": u, "dir": d, "start": a, "stop": z,
                             "light_in": li, "ctrl_in": ci, "light_out": lo, "ctrl_out": co, "light_s_in_field": lt,
                             "home_rate": s["base_rate"][u]})
inf = pd.DataFrame(rows)

inf["gain_out"] = inf.light_out - inf.ctrl_out

      "cells; light time in field per field, median", round(inf.light_s_in_field.median(), 1), "s")

d = inf.gain_in - inf.gain_out
w = stats.wilcoxon(inf.gain_in, inf.gain_out)
print(f"In-field gain higher in {(d > 0).sum()} of {len(d)}; median difference {d.median():.2f} Hz; Wilcoxon p = {w.pvalue:.2g}")
for sess, grp in inf.groupby("session"):
    dd = grp.gain_in - grp.gain_out
    print(f"  {sess}: n = {len(grp)}, median difference {dd.median():.2f}, p = {stats.wilcoxon(grp.gain_in, grp.gain_out).pvalue:.2g}")
ratio_in = inf.light_in / inf.ctrl_in.replace(0, np.nan)

      f"n = {k.sum()}, p = {stats.wilcoxon(ratio_in[k], ratio_out[k]).pvalue:.2g}")

Result: reproduced. Over 80 control place fields of 48 light-responsive putative pyramidal cells, the gain is 3.95 Hz in the field and 1.37 Hz outside it (medians). In-field gain is higher for 61 of 80 fields (Wilcoxon p = 1e-08), and in both sessions (p = 9.5e-07 and 0.0018). As a ratio of light to control rate, the in-field ratio is lower (2.19 against 2.77, p = 4.3e-05), so the increase is larger in hertz but not relative to the control rate.

Result: not reproduced. Over 80 fields, the in-field gain is correlated with neither the out-of-field rate (rho = -0.018, p = 0.87) nor the home-cage rate (rho = -0.063, p = 0.58); both are outside tolerance of 0.17 and 0.25. With one field per cell (48 cells), rho is 0.131 for the out-of-field rate, within tolerance, and -0.003 for the home-cage rate.

Claim fig3a-place-cells-more-excitable¶

Light responses in the home cage before the track were stronger in place cells than in non-place cells (P < 1e-4, Kruskal-Wallis test).

In [20]:
rows = []
for s in opto:
    t = s["resp_table"][s["resp_table"].tested].copy()
    t["resp_hz"] = t.rate_during - t.rate_before
    best = t.groupby("unit").agg(resp_hz=("resp_hz", "max"), z=("z", "max"))
    for u in np.flatnonzero(s["pyr"]):
        rows.append({"session": s["key"].split("_ses-")[1], "unit": u, "place": bool(s["place"][u]),
                     "resp_hz": best.resp_hz.get(u, np.nan), "z": best.z.get(u, np.nan)})
ex = pd.DataFrame(rows).dropna()
for col in ("resp_hz", "z"):
    a, b = ex[ex.place][col], ex[~ex.place][col]
    kw = stats.kruskal(a, b)
    print(f"{col}: place cells n = {len(a)}, median {a.median():.2f}; non-place n = {len(b)}, median {b.median():.2f}; "
          f"Kruskal-Wallis p = {kw.pvalue:.2g}")
for sess, grp in ex.groupby("session"):
    a, b = grp[grp.place].resp_hz, grp[~grp.place].resp_hz
    print(f"  {sess}: place {len(a)} median {a.median():.2f}, non-place {len(b)} median {b.median():.2f}, p = {stats.kruskal(a, b).pvalue:.2g}")
# firing rate as a confound: the comparison within baseline-rate halves
ex["base"] = [s["base_rate"][u] for sess, u in zip(ex.session, ex.unit) for s in opto if s["key"].endswith(sess)]
med = ex.base.median()
for name, part in (("below", ex[ex.base < med]), ("above", ex[ex.base >= med])):
    a, b = part[part.place].resp_hz, part[~part.place].resp_hz
    print(f"  baseline rate {name} the median: place {len(a)} median {a.median():.2f}, non-place {len(b)} median {b.median():.2f}, "
          f"p = {stats.kruskal(a, b).pvalue:.2g}")

Result: not reproduced. In the home cage (PreStim), the light response (rate during the pulse minus before it, best uLED) has a median of 1.90 Hz in 72 place cells and 1.03 Hz in 19 non-place cells, higher in place cells as stated, but not significantly (Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.19; z-scored, p = 0.25). It is significant in sess9 (2.29 against 1.03 Hz, p = 0.027) and not in sess12 (0.94 against 1.19 Hz, p = 0.85). Within halves of the baseline rate neither difference is significant (p = 0.6 and 0.2).

Result: partially reproduced. For 70 field directions of light-responsive place cells (control fields), the light map's peak follows the control map's peak (Pearson r = 0.806, p = 3.9e-17). For 14 field directions of the 7 non-place cells with a light field, r = 0.321 (p = 0.26), so the criterion's test fails for this group. In the shuffle variant, 35.7% of these peaks are within 4.4 cm of the control peak, against 14.6% for shuffled pairings (p = 0.014). Of the 14 unmasked field directions, 8 come from sess9.

Claim fig3f-light-stability¶

Place fields during light stimulation were more stable between the first and second halves of the session than during control epochs, for both true place fields and unmasked place fields (P < 1e-9 and P < 1e-19, two-way ANOVA).

Result: not reproduced. Between laps 11-60 and 71-120, light maps are not more stable than control maps. The medians are 0.664 against 0.714 for place fields (light higher in 28 of 70, p = 0.058) and 0.187 against 0.527 for unmasked fields (light higher in 6 of 14, p = 0.39). Against control maps from as many 20 ms control windows as light windows, light is higher for place fields (0.664 against 0.602) but not significantly (p = 0.68), and lower for unmasked fields (0.187 against 0.293, p = 0.67). Leaving the laps without stimulation out of the control maps gives the same medians (p = 0.059 and 0.39); this variant cannot differ much, since dark windows exist only next to deposited pulses, so laps without stimulation hold almost no control time. The two-way ANOVA finds an effect of condition (p = 0.046), with light the less stable in both groups by the medians above.

Result: partially reproduced. Control and light spatial information are correlated for place fields (rho = 0.655, p = 7.6e-10) and for unmasked fields (rho = 0.574, p = 0.032). The increase from control to light is larger for unmasked fields (median 0.03 bits/spike) than for place fields (-0.03; Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.039), far from the paper's P < 1e-15. Against time-matched control maps the increase is negative in both groups (unmasked -0.17, place -0.10) and does not differ (p = 0.3); as a ratio it does not differ either (1.08 against 0.90, p = 0.14). Unmasked fields are chosen for having a light field and no control field, which favours a larger increase in that group by construction; the paper defines its groups the same way. The paper's control epochs are "random intervals (20 ms) between the light pulses", which the time-matched variant follows most closely, and the dark-window control maps are themselves a revision of the criterion's control (all time with no uLED on). Under the time-matched control both correlations hold (place rho = 0.501, p = 1e-05; unmasked rho = 0.609, p = 0.021) but the increase does not differ between groups, so part 1 holds and part 2 does not. The outcome was changed from reproduced after a third verification round agreed.

Claim fig4c-swr-cofiring-place-pairs¶

Cofiring of place cell pairs during SPW-Rs in the home cage is positively correlated with their spatial overlap on the track (P < 1e-27), while pairs of a place cell and a non-place cell show no such relationship (P = 0.11).

In [26]:
def ripple_counts(s):
    home = [(e["start"], e["stop"]) for e in s["epochs"] if e["behavioral_paradigm"] in ("BaselinePre", "BaselinePost")]
    r = s["ripples"]
    keep = np.zeros(len(r), bool)
    for a, b in home:
        keep |= (r[:, 0] >= a) & (r[:, 1] < b)
    r = r[keep]
    return np.array([np.searchsorted(x, r[:, 1]) - np.searchsorted(x, r[:, 0]) for x in s["spikes"]]), len(r)

pairs = []
for s in opto:
    counts, nrip = ripple_counts(s)
    cof = np.corrcoef(counts)
    s["cofiring"] = cof
    pyr = np.flatnonzero(s["pyr"])
    cmaps = [np.concatenate(s["ctrl_maps"][u]) for u in range(len(s["spikes"]))]
    lmaps = {u: np.concatenate(m) for u, m in s["light_maps"].items()}
    for i_, a in enumerate(pyr):
        for b in pyr[i_ + 1:]:
            kind = {2: "PC-PC", 1: "PC-nonPC", 0: "nonPC-nonPC"}[int(s["place"][a]) + int(s["place"][b])]
            pairs.append({"session": s["key"].split("_ses-")[1], "a": a, "b": b, "kind": kind, "cofiring": cof[a, b],
                          "overlap_ctrl": v.map_corr(cmaps[a], cmaps[b]),
                          "overlap_light": v.map_corr(lmaps[a], lmaps[b]) if (a in lmaps and b in lmaps) else np.nan,
                          "both_responsive": bool(s["responsive"][a] and s["responsive"][b])})
    print(s["key"].split("_ses-")[1], "home-cage ripples without stimulation:", nrip)
pr = pd.DataFrame(pairs)
for kind, k in pr.dropna(subset=["cofiring", "overlap_ctrl"]).groupby("kind"):
    r = stats.spearmanr(k.cofiring, k.overlap_ctrl)
    print(f"{kind}: n = {len(k)} pairs, Spearman rho = {r.statistic:.3f}, p = {r.pvalue:.2g}")
    for sess, kk in k.groupby("session"):
        rr = stats.spearmanr(kk.cofiring, kk.overlap_ctrl)
        print(f"    {sess}: n = {len(kk)}, rho = {rr.statistic:.3f}, p = {rr.pvalue:.2g}")
# Variant: cofiring as the correlation of participation (any spike) per ripple
for s in opto:
    counts, _ = ripple_counts(s)
    s["cofiring_bin"] = np.corrcoef((counts > 0).astype(float))
pr["cofiring_bin"] = [[x for x in opto if x["key"].endswith(r.session)][0]["cofiring_bin"][r.a, r.b] for r in pr.itertuples()]
for kind, k in pr.dropna(subset=["cofiring_bin", "overlap_ctrl"]).groupby("kind"):
    r = stats.spearmanr(k.cofiring_bin, k.overlap_ctrl)
    print(f"Variant, participation correlation, {kind}: n = {len(k)}, rho = {r.statistic:.3f}, p = {r.pvalue:.2g}")
print("Pairs dropped (a cell without spikes in ripples or a flat map):", int(pr[["cofiring", "overlap_ctrl"]].isna().any(axis=1).sum()))

Result: reproduced. Over 1264 place cell pairs, cofiring during home-cage ripples is correlated with spatial overlap (Spearman rho = 0.060, p = 0.032), weakly and in sess9 only (rho = 0.119, p = 0.0015; sess12 rho = 0.019, p = 0.66). Over 698 pairs of a place cell and a non-place cell, the paper's test finds no correlation (rho = 0.062, p = 0.1), as in the paper, but the coefficient is as large as for place cell pairs, so the absence comes from fewer pairs, not a weaker relation. Participation per ripple gives rho = 0.054 (p = 0.056) and 0.072 (p = 0.058). The cofiring measure is this attempt's choice; the paper's is in the supplement.

Blocked claims: what the files hold¶

The stored value of every pulse series is printed in the data check (one value per uLED), as are the units table's columns. Below, a proxy for figs9-excitatory-vs-inhibitory-swr, shown for the verifier and not deciding its outcome.

In [28]:
# Proxy for figs9: units at or above 5 Hz in the first epoch as putative interneurons, against
# the putative pyramidal cells, by the log2 ratio of the rate inside deposited ripples to the
# rate outside (first epoch, sessions with at least 50 ripples there), as in figs10.
rows = []
for s in sessions:
    e0 = s["epochs"][0]
    r = s["ripples"]
    r = r[(r[:, 0] >= e0["start"]) & (r[:, 1] < e0["stop"])]
    if len(r) < 50:
        continue
    t_in = (r[:, 1] - r[:, 0]).sum()
    t_out = (e0["stop"] - e0["start"]) - t_in
    for u, x in enumerate(s["spikes"]):
        n_all = ((x >= e0["start"]) & (x < e0["stop"])).sum()
        n_in = (np.searchsorted(x, r[:, 1]) - np.searchsorted(x, r[:, 0])).sum()
        if n_in > 0 and n_all > n_in:
            rows.append({"pyr": bool(s["pyr"][u]), "log2_ratio": np.log2((n_in / t_in) / ((n_all - n_in) / t_out))})
px = pd.DataFrame(rows)
a, b = px[px.pyr].log2_ratio, px[~px.pyr].log2_ratio
print(f"Putative pyramidal (below 5 Hz): n = {len(a)}, median log2 ratio {a.median():.2f}; units at or above 5 Hz: "
      f"n = {len(b)}, median {b.median():.2f}; Mann-Whitney p = {stats.mannwhitneyu(a, b).pvalue:.2g}")

Putative pyramidal (below 5 Hz): n = 1166, median log2 ratio 1.19; units at or above 5 Hz: n = 121, median 0.75; Mann-Whitney p = 0.00065

Units at or above 5 Hz raise their rate inside ripples less than the putative pyramidal cells (median log2 ratio 0.75 against 1.19, p = 0.00065), in the direction of the claim. The split is by baseline rate, and within the putative pyramidal cells alone the ripple gain falls with baseline rate (figs10, rho = -0.437), so a split by rate would show this with no interneurons among the faster units. The claim stays blocked.

Summary¶

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

How the analysis differs from the paper's. The Materials and Methods were not available. The light-response test is the one in the first author's later code, the place fields use a port of buzcode's bz_findPlaceFields1D with its defaults, and the theta phase, cofiring and stability measures are common choices. Pyramidal cells are units with a baseline rate below 5 Hz, as the files carry no cell type. Every claim on light responses or place fields rests on 2 sessions of one mouse (91 putative pyramidal cells), the only sessions with pulse times, against the paper's 822 cells. Most pulses are not in the files, so control time is restricted to the windows that the stated protocol keeps dark (the 20 ms before each deposited onset and after each offset); all time without a deposited pulse is shown as a variant. Cells on the shank whose uLEDs are missing cannot be tested for light responses. The dark windows assume every offset between pulses is at least 20 ms; 3% to 4% of the deposited offsets are shorter.

What was found about the dandiset.

  • Pulse times are in 2 of 28 sessions; 20 more sessions name uLED stimulation in their epochs but hold no pulse times, so their light responses cannot be computed. Laps are also in these 2 only.
  • The pulse series are stated in watts but hold one arbitrary value per uLED (19 in one session, about 63000 in the other). They carry no light intensity, so the intensity results cannot be tested. The files hold series for 6 of the probe's 12 uLEDs, and the deposited pulses are about a third of those the protocol implies (5.76 and 7.50 per s); no cell on one shank responds to any deposited uLED.
  • Every session is deposited twice, as a full file and a no-raw-data file with the same units, spikes, ripples and position. One full file lacks the session in its name. The full file of fCamk3 sess17 holds 378 s of raw signal and 6850 s of LFP of a 34621 s session, and six fCamk1 full files have no raw signal.
  • Units carry no cell type and the small files no waveforms.
  • session_start_time is 2016-03-15 in every file, though the sessions are from 2020 and 2021.
  • The linearized position has a conversion factor of 100 with values already in cm.
  • Six sessions have epochs without paradigm or manipulation. 14 sessions include CNO or DMSO epochs, which the paper does not describe. The dandiset holds 28 sessions and 1351 putative pyramidal cells, where the paper reports 822 cells (about 19 sessions), and does not say which sessions the paper used.
  • In three sessions the deposited ripple intervals mark population bursts weakly; fCamk2 has 0 to 1110 ripples per session and no position.
  • The file description of the pulses gives 40 to 60 ms offsets, the paper 20 to 40 ms.
  • The paper reports 417 non-place cells among 822 pyramidal neurons (51%), while 73% of responsive and 71% of non-responsive neurons are place cells, which leaves about 230 non-place cells.
